telegram.title: Telegram
telegram.description: The bot you use to talk to the super agent. It is configured in .env; this page only shows its status.
telegram.statusDescription: Values read from .env by the web server. The worker reads them at startup.
telegram.tokenMissing: missing: the bot does not start
telegram.noUsers: no users: the bot refuses everyone
telegram.notifyFallback: not set, notifications go to <mono>{target}</mono> (the first allowed user)
telegram.topicsDescription: Projects with a telegramTopicId get their notifications in their own topic, and messages written there run in the project context.
telegram.topicsEmpty: No project has a topic configured ({count, plural, one {# project} other {# projects}} in total). Set the topic ID on the project page.
telegram.step1: Open <mono>@BotFather</mono> in Telegram, send <mono>/newbot</mono> and copy the token into <mono>TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN</mono> in .env.
telegram.step2: Restart the worker. The bot commands ({commands}) are set automatically at startup, no need for <mono>/setcommands</mono>.
telegram.step3: To find your ID, send any message to the bot in private: if you are not on the list, it replies with your Telegram ID. Add it to <mono>TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_IDS</mono> (several IDs separated by commas) and restart the worker.
telegram.step4: Optional, for notifications in a group: set <mono>TELEGRAM_NOTIFY_CHAT_ID</mono> to the group ID. Without it, notifications go to the private chat with the first allowed user.
telegram.step5: For one topic per project: create a group with Topics (forum) enabled, add the bot as an administrator, set the group ID in <mono>TELEGRAM_NOTIFY_CHAT_ID</mono>, create a topic for each project and save the topic ID (message_thread_id, the last number in the link of a message from the topic) in the project settings.
telegram.transcriptionDescription: Voice messages are transcribed with OpenAI, so they need the OpenAI key.
